idiom_name: typed accessor with a cached private field
implementation_notes: TypeScript has no lazy member of its own, so the stand-in is an accessor: `get image(): Image` constructs on the first read and stores the result in a private field typed as `Image | undefined`, which keeps the uninitialized state out of the public type; TypeScript 4.3+ also allows the getter and setter to carry different types. The structural type system means the stand-in only has to be assignable to the interface, so no class hierarchy is required, and a Proxy object with a get trap is the dynamic alternative when the deferred member is not known statically. The explicit class is still justified when one stand-in must forward several methods and preserve readonly or record-like semantics.
pitfalls: Accessors live on the prototype, so the cached value must be an own instance property; a class field declared without an initializer only stays undefined until the accessor fills it, and sharing state in a closure would cache one value for all instances.
Serialization round trips (JSON.parse, Object.assign, structuredClone) strip the prototype and the cached field, leaving a plain object that has neither the deferred member nor the guard.
Structural typing accepts any compatible shape, so a stand-in that forgets identity operations (equals, toString, a discriminated tag) still type-checks and then misbehaves at runtime.
